context:
This item asks you to pick how a ruling names the earlier ruling it overtakes. It stops nothing: the lane builds on what exists meanwhile.
Goal: the later-ruling check can find overtaken rulings without guessing from prose.
Problem (rule): the ruled store has a field `supersedes` (a list of the things a ruling replaces), but no field names the overtaken ruling by id: a `ruling`-kind ref is free prose. So the check falls back to prose words. That is the cry-wolf shape of PR 3476, the held PR whose word matching fired on common words (6 of 8 process Departs lines hit 3 to 26 rulings).
Based on (read): lane's read, relayed by the coordinator at 11:27 CST Nov 15, not read by triage. The incident ruling is own-820-c-five-repos. The record-vs-later-ruling lane read `git show origin/roadmap:roadmap/rulings/own-820-c-five-repos.json` (keys id, at, title, ruling, quote, source, status, step: no `supersedes`, no `supersedes_none`). Running `python3 lint/ruled_store.py check .` on origin/roadmap at 11:08 CST flags it ("neither supersedes nor supersedes_none is set"; 322 lines in all, 273 of that kind). The coordinator's "had neither" was that measured read.
Based on (read): decision ruled-store-one-home, line 13, and check_entry (lint/ruled_store.py): a new entry needs a non-empty `supersedes` list or a non-empty `supersedes_none` reason. Nothing runs `check` on the whole store today (the decision's own text says so), so older entries lack the field unchecked. A `ruling`-kind ref is free prose (drop-nightly-schedule: "R61 nightly skip when main's newest commit is green (...)"); ruled_store.py reads only the first token of such a ref, for the shared-ref check. The lane agrees ruling refs are free prose. Earlier text of this item called the coordinator's reading unmatched and unmeasured; that was wrong, and is corrected here.
Based on (ruling): none found. Searched origin/roadmap roadmap/rulings, docs/decisions and lint/ruled_store.py for supersedes, supersedes_none and overtake: no ruling says a ruling that overtakes one must name it, or that a ref must hold an id.
Departs from: main (check_entry asks a new entry for `supersedes` or `supersedes_none`, any `supersedes_none` text passes, a `ruling` ref is free prose, and no check runs over the whole store) — option A: a `ruling` ref must begin with the id of an entry in the store, and a ruling that overtakes an earlier one must list it; option B changes nothing.
Who recommends what: option A is the coordinator's recommendation, not yours. Neither option widens what a shared tool accepts: A makes check_entry stricter, B leaves it as is. Limit of A: whether a ruling overtakes another stays a human judgment at filing; the check can only keep the ref well formed.

lastAnswer.note: what diffs old prs from new ones in a sense to confirm they dont just share a similar name

options.gain: The check keys on a field, so it can name the overtaken ruling without word guessing, and the false alarms of PR 3476's shape stop.
options.how: A ruling that overtakes an earlier ruling lists it in `supersedes`, kind `ruling`, with that ruling's id as the first token of the ref. check_entry refuses a `ruling` ref whose first token is no id in the store. The later-ruling check reads the field, not prose.
options.label: Require the overtaken ruling's id in `supersedes` (recommended by the coordinator)
options.lose: One more checked field per overtaking ruling, and triage must fill it at filing. The check cannot tell that a ruling overtakes one, so a missed field stays missed.

options.gain: No new field and no new refusal for triage's filing.
options.how: No change to the store. The later-ruling check keeps reading words in the ruling text when no field names the overtaken ruling.
options.label: Leave the prose fallback
options.lose: False alarms risk: matching on prose is the shape that cried wolf in PR 3476, and a cry-wolf check is spent.
